newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended mixed after a favourable reception to the Federal government's latest auction which reopened an existing 4-1/2 percent 2007 bond.
Swiss dealers were positive about the issue.
"It came in quite well," said Caspar Ruetz, head of government trade at UBS. "I think it is a brilliant bond, you have to have it," Ruetz added.

Strong volume was generated by investors switching out of more expensive 2008 and 2006 maturities. Demand for the new paper was fed by steepness in the Swiss yield curve, which has led investors to seek higher yields in the long end.
The new bond was priced at 105.45 to yield 3.849 percent at issue SWIW.

A spokesman for the Swiss Federal Treasury in Berne said the market had been strong recently and this had helped demand. Allocation on Thursday of 904 million Swiss francs brought the outstanding amount to 2.43 billion Swiss francs.

The bond is deliverable against the Conf futures contract. Some traders said earlier this week that there had been a shortage of deliverable paper for the Conf contract, which also was likely to have spurred demand for the new paper.
The Canton of Geneva also set a 250 million franc bond.
That bond, for 10 years with a coupon of four percent, was quoted yielding 4.06 percent.
The short end was weaker, but some traders believe it also had room to improve, especially if the Swiss franc can gain ground versus the dollar after latest declines.
The Swiss National Bank, as expected, left its discount rate at 1.00 percent after a regular weekly meeting of its board on Thursday. No change was expected in the rate.
March Conf futures CONFH7 down three at 117.65.
March Comi medium-term bond COMIH7 steady at 111.60
Mar Euro Swiss francs FESH7 down five at 98.15.
